purpose: Human-reviewed Ghana-focused cases for testing evidence-based assessments independently of model predictions.

assessment_definitions.likely_real: The central claim is supported by the cited professional review and its documented evidence.
assessment_definitions.likely_fake: The central claim is contradicted by the cited professional review and its documented evidence.
assessment_definitions.misleading: The claim contains accurate material but presents it with an incorrect date, context, attribution or implication.
assessment_definitions.partly_true: The claim contains both supported and unsupported factual elements.
assessment_definitions.corrected: The original publication or source acknowledged and corrected a material error.
assessment_definitions.retracted: The publisher withdrew the original claim or publication after determining that it was inaccurate.

cases.claim: The 2025 budget projected overall real GDP growth of about 4 percent, below the 5.7 percent recorded for 2024.
cases.public_reason: The 2025 budget set overall real GDP growth at 4.0 percent, while official statistics recorded 5.7 percent growth for 2024.

cases.claim: Most Hepatitis B cases in Ghana are not transmitted sexually.
cases.public_reason: Ghana Health Service guidance and published research identify mother-to-child transmission as the principal route in high-prevalence settings such as Ghana.

cases.claim: Ghana's 2025 budgetary allocation for basic education was the highest in a decade.
cases.public_reason: Budget and appropriation records from 2016 through 2025 show that the 2025 basic-education allocation was the largest during the ten-year period reviewed.

cases.claim: More than 21 million Ghanaians could not afford a healthy diet.
evidence_basis: FAO State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2025 report
cases.public_reason: The FAO's 2025 food-security report estimated that 22.9 million people in Ghana could not afford a healthy diet in 2024.

cases.claim: The Government of Ghana cancelled the Free Senior High School programme in 2025.
cases.public_reason: The cited education memorandum concerned procurement of school items and did not cancel Free SHS; official statements confirmed that the programme remained in operation.

cases.claim: Ghana integrated payments into the Ghana Card and abandoned Visa and Mastercard.
cases.claimant: Social-media users and a news website
evidence_basis: functional check of the cited shortcode
cases.public_reason: The National Identification Authority stated that payment integration had not been completed, and the cited shortcode did not provide payment functions.

cases.claim: The Ghana Revenue Authority reintroduced the Electronic Transfer Levy in May 2026.
cases.public_reason: The charge was a proposed MTN service fee rather than a government tax, and the Bank of Ghana directed the company to pause its implementation.

cases.claim: Ghana had already exited its International Monetary Fund programme on 1 January 2026.
cases.public_reason: The President said Ghana was beginning the process of leaving the programme; official programme information showed that IMF support was still active at that date.

cases.claim: Mahamudu Bawumia received a new appointment to a United Nations board in January 2025.
evidence_basis: 2018 Ghana Mission to the United Nations publication
dated reports of the original appointment
cases.public_reason: The appointment was genuine but occurred in 2018; recirculating the old announcement as a new appointment in 2025 removed its original date and context.

cases.claim: President John Mahama appointed Justice Paul Baffoe-Bonnie as acting Chief Justice in April 2025.
cases.public_reason: The Constitution assigns the Chief Justice's functions automatically to the most senior Supreme Court justice when the officeholder cannot serve; the President did not make this acting appointment.

cases.claim: Ghana's trade balance moved from minus 2.3 percent in 2016 to 4.6 percent in 2024.
cases.public_reason: The 4.6 percent figure for October 2024 was supported, but official records placed the 2016 trade balance at minus 4.0 percent rather than minus 2.3 percent.

cases.claim: Non-communicable diseases account for exactly 42 percent of all deaths in Ghana.
cases.public_reason: Available health evidence places the proportion at approximately 42 to 45 percent, so the claim is broadly supported but presents an estimate as an exact figure.

cases.claim: Joseph Siaw Agyepong received specified procurement deals and was under criminal investigation in connection with them.
cases.public_reason: GhanaWeb withdrew the references after determining that the procurement and criminal-investigation claims concerning Joseph Siaw Agyepong were inaccurate.

cases.claim: Justice Nene Amegatcher said that the removal of Chief Justice Gertrude Torkornoo was questionable.
cases.public_reason: The Ghanaian Chronicle acknowledged that the statement attributed to Justice Nene Amegatcher was inaccurate and retracted the publication in full.

cases.claim: Frank Oliver Kpodo personally received GH¢427,995,661.40 in unearned salary payments.
cases.public_reason: The Auditor-General identified a transpositional error and clarified that the amount concerned payroll anomalies involving 3,476 staff rather than money received by Frank Oliver Kpodo.

cases.claim: A photograph released during a GoldBod briefing showed gold-smuggling suspect Mohammed Nandoli Rafeeq.
cases.public_reason: GoldBod acknowledged that the photograph showed a different person, apologised and issued the correct image of the suspect.
